topic: How does antenna design influence the accuracy of encrypted traffic classification systems in heterogeneous satellite networks?
consensus_response: The design of antennas in satellite networks significantly influences the accuracy of encrypted traffic classification. Higher gain and directivity can enhance signal strength and reduce interference, but they also narrow the beamwidth, potentially missing weaker signals. Polarization mismatch can introduce additional noise, degrading classification accuracy. In complex propagation environments, these factors interact to affect signal integrity and reliability, thereby impacting the performance of ML models used for traffic classification. Optimizing antenna parameters is crucial for balancing signal quality and interference, ensuring robust classification in heterogeneous satellite networks. Advanced antenna technologies like phased arrays and metamaterial-based antennas can further enhance signal quality, reduce interference, and improve frequency agility, leading to more accurate and efficient traffic classification.
